transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well… mostly it’s that I can’t seem to keep things in order anymore at work. I work with laundry and dry cleaning, so there are tickets, receipts, little notes from the workshop, customer jobs, all these things that have to match up and be kept straight. And lately it just feels like everything ends up in one pile, or several piles, and then I’m standing there trying to figure out what I’m supposed to handle first.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because it’s not like I don’t know the work. I’ve done this kind of thing a long time. But I’ll have a customer job, then a receipt tucked somewhere, then notes about what needs special handling, and somehow they all get mixed together. Then I’m sorting and re-sorting instead of just doing the next thing. That’s really what made me come in—things feel disorganized in a way I can’t seem to get back under control.
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty keeping things organized and staying on task going back to when you were a kid or teenager, or is this something that's really only started recently?

No, it definitely goes way back. I mean, I didn’t think of it that way when I was young, of course, but looking back… yes. Even in grade school my teachers used to tell my mother things like, “She’s bright, but she’s scattered,” or “She knows the material, but she doesn’t finish what she starts.” That kind of thing.

I remember losing papers all the time, or having them crumpled up somewhere in my desk or my bag, and then I’d swear I had done the work but couldn’t find it. And teachers were always reminding me to finish, to get back to the assignment, to stop talking—because I’d talk out of turn without really meaning to. It wasn’t that I was trying to be rude. I’d just have something in my head and it would come out before I thought about whether it was my turn.

So… no, it’s not brand new. It feels worse now because the stakes at work are different, but that “bright but scattered” thing has been there since I was a kid.
Aside from the disorganization, have you been feeling persistently worried, on edge, or tense recently?

I don’t know that I’d call it persistently worried exactly. I mean, I get bothered when things are piling up or when I know I’ve misplaced something, because then I’m standing there thinking, “Oh no, where did that go?” But it’s more like frustration in the moment than walking around tense all day.

I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by worried or on edge. I wouldn’t say I wake up feeling dread or anything like that. It’s more that when I’m already behind or things are out of place, then I get flustered. But outside of those situations, I don’t think of myself as constantly anxious.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a change in your mood—like feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

Not really, no… I don’t think I’ve had a big change in my mood like that. I mean, I get upset with myself when I’m making a mess of things at work or when I can’t find something I know I just had, but that feels more like aggravation or embarrassment than being sad all the time.

As far as enjoying things, I haven’t really noticed that everything feels flat or pointless or anything like that. I still like the things I usually like when I’m not caught up in the work mess. So… no, over the last couple weeks I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down in that way.

Aside from the organizational issues we've discussed, have you noticed any new problems with your memory or thinking clearly—like forgetting recent conversations or feeling more confused than usual—that seem different from how you've always been?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I forget things, but it feels like the same kind of forgetting I’ve always done—like putting something down and then immediately not knowing where I put it, or walking into the back room and thinking, “What was I coming in here for?” But that’s not really new for me.

I haven’t noticed myself forgetting whole conversations or feeling confused about where I am or what I’m doing, nothing like that. It’s more like my mind jumps ahead or gets pulled in different directions, and then I lose track of the thing I was supposed to be holding onto. But I wouldn’t say my thinking feels different lately. It’s frustrating, but it feels like the same pattern, not some new memory problem.
